name: Web Protocols

control.title: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service

evidence.rationale: Adversaries use web protocols to blend with normal traffic. A server firewall can partially restrict which destinations, ports, and web services a server may contact, though it will not stop all HTTP/S abuse.
Destination-aware or application-aware firewall restrictions can disrupt web-based command and control, but basic port filtering cannot distinguish malicious traffic from legitimate browsing.
DNS filtering can prevent HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket command-and-control connections when the destination domain has been classified as malicious.

Adversaries use HTTP or HTTPS to communicate with command-and-control infrastructure. Default-deny Internet egress on dedicated administrative resources prevents direct connections to external HTTP/S C2 infrastructure, directly disrupting the communication channel.

Restrict HTTP and HTTPS traffic crossing network-segment boundaries from critical systems to approved destinations, reducing unauthorized outbound web communications used for command and control or payload transfer.
Network intrusion prevention solutions can use signatures for malicious HTTP or HTTPS traffic associated with specific adversary tools to block command-and-control activity at the network boundary.
Web proxies and application-layer firewalls can inspect and restrict HTTP and HTTPS traffic to unauthorized or malicious destinations.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
